source.snippet: A playlist has 124 videos. My tool imported 15, then 100, then finally 124. One of my extension's features imports a whole YouTube playlist into your notebook in one click. (score: 9, 1 comment, Aug 2026, tags: buildinpublic, startup, sass, webdev)

problem_statement: Users want to reliably import entire YouTube playlists (and their metadata) into note-taking or knowledge management tools in one click, but existing browser extensions and tools fail silently or partially import content, requiring multiple retries and manual fixes.
target_segment: Content creators, researchers, students, and knowledge workers who use YouTube heavily and maintain digital notebooks or PKM tools
notes: Dev.to builder post describing a real reliability problem with a paying-user product (tagged 'sass'). Score of 9 suggests resonance. Buyer signal moderate — notebook/PKM tools are paid category (Notion, Obsidian Sync, Roam). The reliability gap (15 → 100 → 124 videos) is a concrete, recurring engineering pain that the market hasn't fully solved.
